review_note: Corrected original DOI from unrelated Lifshin 2017 study to explicitly cited Lifshin et al. 2018. Original abstract on author university site; replication publisher abstract is cached in frozen packet. Same curvilinear attitude effect, sample and measure are conceptual replication.

replication_title: Generality of Creativity across Performance Domains: A Replication
effect_name: Creativity shows little generality across performance domains
effect_claim: Creative performance scores across different kinds of products were not correlated after accounting for IQ and academic achievement.
effect_claim_quote: When the effects of IQ reading achievement, and math achievement were controlled through multiple regression analyses, creativity scores on the four tasks were not correlated.
original_title: Generality of creativity across performance domains

effect_claim: The teacher-led Dove Confident Me lesson improved some short-term body image and eating outcomes.
effect_claim_quote: post-intervention improvements for intervention students relative to control in body esteem (TL; girls only)
original_title: Effectiveness of a brief school-based body image intervention ‘Dove Confident Me: Single Session’ when delivered by teachers and researchers: Results from a cluster randomised controlled trial
replication_title: Independent pragmatic replication of the Dove Confident Me body image program in an Australian Girls Independent Secondary School
replication_target_quote: this research aimed to investigate whether the universal co-educational prevention program developed for audiences in the United Kingdom (Dove Confident Me, DCM), was an acceptable and effective intervention
outcome_quote: No improvements were observed on outcome measures between the comparison and intervention girls over the three time points.
review_note: Independent pragmatic replication in a single-sex Australian school found no measured benefit; setting and delivery differ from the original trial.

effect_name: Personality dimensions correlate with social attitudes
effect_claim: Neuroticism and psychoticism correlated with particular social attitudes in the original sample.
effect_claim_quote: Neuroticism was related to ethnocentrism and the intolerance of minority groups
original_title: SOCIAL ATTITUDE CORRELATES OF EYSENCK'S PERSONALITY DIMENSIONS
original_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_title: IS PERSONALITY RELATED TO SOCIAL ATTITUDES? AN ATTEMPT AT REPLICATION
replication_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_target_quote: An attempt was made to replicate previous work relating Eysenck's personality dimensions to social attitudes.
outcome_quote: No significant correlation was obtained between psychoticism, neuroticism, extraversion, Lie Scale, and any of the six social attitude variables.
review_note: The later paper explicitly attempts replication in student nurses and finds none of the original personality-attitude correlations in that sample.

effect_name: Missing intake information predicts suicidal thinking
effect_claim: Missing demographic answers on client intake forms indicate greater severity of suicidal thinking.
effect_claim_quote: missing information on education, income, and/or number of persons living with the respondent were valid indicators of the severity of suicidal thinking
original_title: Does the Fact that a Client has Failed to Provide Requested Information Predict Severity of Suicidal Thinking?: A Criterion Validity Study of Missing Client Information
replication_title: The Criterion Validity of Omitted Client Information as an Indicator of Suicide Risk: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: replicate findings reported by Nugent and Williams-Hayes that suggested that there is a relationship between missing information on demographic items found on client intake forms and severity of suicidal ideation
outcome_quote: The results partially replicated those of Nugent and Williams-Hayes
review_note: The later study explicitly retests the original intake-form finding and reports only partial replication.

effect_name: Parents favor aerobic over strength exercise for adolescents
effect_claim: Parents view aerobic exercise for their children more favorably than strength exercise.
effect_claim_quote: Parents consistently reported a positive attitude towards aerobic exercises, but a less positive attitude regarding strength exercises.
original_title: Aerobic and strength exercises for youngsters aged 12 to 15: what do parents think?
replication_title: Turkish Parents’ Attitudes Towards Strength and Aerobic Exercises in their Children: A Replication of Ten Hoor et al. (2015)
replication_target_quote: a Dutch study by ten Hoor et al. (2015) was replicated in Turkey
outcome_quote: Turkish parents had more positive attitudes for aerobic exercises compared to strength exercises.
review_note: The later Turkish parent survey explicitly repeats the Dutch study and finds the same difference in attitudes.

effect_name: Anhedonia predicts suicidal thinking beyond depression
effect_claim: Anhedonia was associated with suicidal ideation after accounting for other depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: Anhedonia was associated with suicidal ideation, even when accounting for depressive symptoms.
original_title: The Association between Anhedonia, Suicidal Ideation, and Suicide Attempts in a Large Student Sample
replication_title: The Association Between Anhedonia, Suicide Ideation, and Suicide Attempts: A Replication in a Persian Student Sample
replication_target_quote: this study attempted to replicate a recent anhedonia and suicide study (conducted in a western culture) in a Persian sample
outcome_quote: anhedonia was associated with suicide risk, even when it was statistically accounting for other depressive symptoms.
review_note: Cross-cultural replication in a Persian student sample retains the association after accounting for other depressive symptoms.

effect_name: Brief habit reversal reduces public-speaking disfluencies
effect_claim: Brief habit reversal training reduced speech disfluencies during public speaking.
effect_claim_quote: Brief habit reversal combined with an interdependent group contingency resulted in a meaningful reduction in speech disfluencies
original_title: Using brief habit reversal and an interdependent group contingency to reduce public‐speaking speech disfluencies
replication_title: Using Brief Habit Reversal to Decrease Speech Disfluencies in Public Speaking. A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: The study was systematically replicated to evaluate the benefit of brief habit reversal training for social workers in decreasing speech disfluencies.
outcome_quote: all participants reduced speech disfluencies during brief habit reversal.
review_note: Later systematic replication in social-work students reports reduced disfluencies during the training and sustained improvement.

effect_name: Internal locus of control predicts small-group leadership
effect_claim: Students who became task leaders tended to have a more internal locus of control than followers.
effect_claim_quote: Task leaders tended to show a belief in internal control and followers a belief in external control.
original_title: Status-Role Consequences of Internal-External Control of Reinforcement
replication_title: Replications of Association between Internal Locus of Control and Leadership in Small Groups
replication_target_quote: An internal locus of control, as measured by Rotter's ( 5 ) internal-external (I-E) scale has been associated (2 ) with sociometrically determined task-leadership
outcome_quote: leaders tended to be more external than followers, although this was not statistically significant
review_note: Later authors explicitly retest their earlier small-group result with matched participants; the leadership association does not repeat.

effect_name: Men receive more and longer newspaper obituaries
effect_claim: Men were more likely than women to receive obituaries and photographs, and women’s obituaries were shorter.
effect_claim_quote: A disproportionately low number of women received obituaries, and female obituaries were also shorter.
original_title: Sex Discrimination after Death
original_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_title: Sex Discrimination after Death: A Replication, Extension and a Difference
replication_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_target_quote: The present work is an extension of that initiated by Kastenbaum, Peyton and Kastenbaum on subtle expressions of sex discrimination after death.
outcome_quote: The earlier work of Kastenbaum and his associates is weakly confirmed
review_note: Denver obituaries show some male excess, but differences lessen or disappear across time and after accounting for occupational content.

effect_name: Most child-maltreatment studies omit ethnicity from analysis
effect_claim: Most child-maltreatment research papers in the sampled journals did not use ethnicity in analyses.
effect_claim_quote: three quarters of the articles published in the most recent years examined (1995-1998) did not include ethnicity in their analyses or design.
original_title: Ethnicity in Child Maltreatment Research: A Content Analysis
replication_title: Ethnicity in Child Maltreatment Research: A Replication of Behl et al.'s Content Analysis
replication_target_quote: Ethnicity in Child Maltreatment Research: A Replication of Behl et al.'s Content Analysis
outcome_quote: 33.8% use ethnicity of participants in analyses
review_note: Later content analysis repeats the journal survey; it finds greater inclusion than the original, yet most articles still omit ethnicity from analysis.

effect_name: Future-oriented web searches track regional GDP
effect_claim: Places with more searches about the future relative to the past tend to have higher GDP.
effect_claim_quote: We analyse Google logs and find a striking correlation between the country's GDP and the predisposition of its inhabitants to look forward.
original_title: Quantifying the Advantage of Looking Forward
replication_title: Seeking Forward, Looking Forward: A Replication and Generalization of the Future Orientation Index Utilizing Baidu Index
replication_target_quote: Our study aimed to replicate and extend correlations between the FOI and key development indicators, such as GDP and Human Development Index (HDI)
outcome_quote: Our results successfully replicated the correlation between the Baidu-based FOI and province-level GDP
review_note: The later study repeats the future-orientation index using Baidu and finds a group-level GDP association; it separately reports no individual-level patience prediction.

effect_name: First-trial versus all-trials measurement in autism treatment
effect_claim: Measuring only the first trial generally indicated quicker skill acquisition, while measuring every trial indicated stronger maintenance.
effect_claim_quote: When differences were detected, quicker acquisition was typically associated with discontinuous measurement, and stronger maintenance was typically associated with continuous measurement.
original_title: EVALUATING PROGRESS IN BEHAVIORAL PROGRAMS FOR CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDERS VIA CONTINUOUS AND DISCONTINUOUS MEASUREMENT
replication_title: COMPARISON OF DATA‐COLLECTION METHODS IN A BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION PROGRAM FOR CHILDREN WITH PERVASIVE DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS: A REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: Cummings and Carr (2009) compared two methods of data collection in a behavioral intervention program for children with pervasive developmental disorders: collecting data on all trials versus only the first trial in a session.
outcome_quote: In the current replication, no such differences in indication of mastery or maintenance were observed when data were collected on all trials or the first trial.
review_note: OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2068866708). Original and replication both 2009, original Spring/March precedes replication Winter/December.

effect_name: Glucose and fructose boosts to anagram solving
effect_claim: Consuming glucose or fructose before an anagram task increased the number of anagrams solved relative to placebo.
effect_claim_quote: It was observed that consuming fructose and glucose resulted in the resolution of more anagrams than the placebo.
original_title: Can you enhance executive control without glucose? The effects of fructose on problem solving
replication_title: What Enables Self-Control? A Test of Glucose, Fructose, and Vagus Nerve Activation as Possible Factors
replication_target_quote: This study replicated the study by Miller, Bourrasseau, and Blampain (2013) on the effects of fructose and glucose on\nself-control.
outcome_quote: it was found that fructose, glucose, and VM did not increase the participants' levels of self-control
review_note: OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2149227176). Published article; later full text explicitly cites Miller, Bourrasseau, and Blampain (2013).

replication_title: Plasticity in older adults’ theory of mind performance: the impact of motivation
effect_name: Closeness motivation removes older adults’ faux pas recognition deficit
effect_claim: Older adults whose sense of closeness to the experimenter was increased performed as well as younger adults on faux pas recognition.
effect_claim_quote: When closeness was experimentally increased, older adults enhanced their performance, and they now performed at a comparable level as younger adults.
original_title: Perspective taking in older age revisited: A motivational perspective
replication_target_quote: Following a previous paradigm, 171 Chinese adults (87 younger adults and 84 older adults) were recruited, and we experimentally manipulated the level of perceived closeness between participants and the experimenter before administering the ToM tasks in order to enhance participants' motivation.
outcome_quote: Results showed that, for the Faux Pas task, we replicated previous findings such that older adults under the enhanced motivation conditions performed equally well as younger adults.
review_note: Corrected to Zhang et al. 2013 Study 1: same lead author, closeness manipulation and faux-pas task. Later primary PDF methods explicitly cite Zhang et al. 2013 Study 1 and reference DOI 10.1037/a0031211. Narrows effect to faux-pas age-gap attenuation; animation task did not generalize.

effect_name: Posted speed feedback reduces speeding
effect_claim: Public signs showing the share of drivers obeying the speed limit reduced speeding.
effect_claim_quote: public posting was highly effective in reducing the percentage of speeding drivers
original_title: A COMPARISON OF THE EFFECTS OF POSTED FEEDBACK AND INCREASED POLICE SURVEILLANCE ON HIGHWAY SPEEDING
replication_title: A REPLICATION OF THE USE OF PUBLIC POSTING IN TRAFFIC SPEED CONTROL
replication_target_quote: a reversal design was used to assess the effects of publicly posted feedback on vehicle speed reduction
outcome_quote: Results from the two feedback conditions indicated no speed reduction in comparison to baseline levels.
review_note: The later paper explicitly cites the 1981 Van Houten and Nau study among the public-posting experiments it retests; its two feedback conditions did not reduce speeding.

effect_name: Triggers for change and coping differ
effect_claim: The life events that prompt change are not associated with events that prompt coping.
effect_claim_quote: stimuli that prompt change were not associated with the stimuli that prompt coping
original_title: The experience of changing and the relationship between changing and coping: an adult perspective
replication_title: Changing and coping, and the stimulus to change from an adolescent perspective: A replication of adult research
replication_target_quote: The aims of this research is to replicate an adult study
outcome_quote: There was no association between what the adolescents reported as stimuli to change and the stimuli to cope.
review_note: Same authors repeat their change-versus-coping interview study among adolescents and again find no association between the two reported sets of triggers.

effect_name: European suicide rates form a geographic J-shaped pattern
effect_claim: Latitude and its interaction with longitude account for substantial variation in European suicide rates.
effect_claim_quote: The interaction term explains 40.8% and 29.1% of men's and women's suicide rate, respectively
original_title: The Finno-Ugrian Suicide Hypothesis: Variation in European Suicide Rates by Latitude and Longitude
replication_title: Testing the Finno-Ugrian Suicide Hypothesis: Replication and Refinement with Regional Suicide Data from Eastern Europe
replication_target_quote: The present research replicated and extended 2003 findings of Voracek, Fisher, and Marusic with new data.
outcome_quote: an interaction term of squared latitude multiplied with longitude (quantifying the J-shaped belt) accounted for 32% of the cross-national variance in total suicide rates alone
review_note: The same authors rerun the geographic correlation with newer and regional data. This records a spatial association, not a genetic explanation.

effect_name: Test-anxiety worry relates to expected performance
effect_claim: The worry component of test anxiety is more strongly related to performance expectancy than emotionality.
effect_claim_quote: W was found to be negatively related to expectancy. E was not consistently related to expectancy
original_title: Cognitive and Emotional Components of Test Anxiety: Temporal Factors
replication_title: Worry and Emotionality as Components of Test Anxiety: Replication and Further Data
replication_target_quote: Worry and Emotionality as Components of Test Anxiety: Replication and Further Data
outcome_quote: W was more highly correlated with expectancy of success ratings than E
review_note: The later test-anxiety paper again finds worry more related to expected success than emotionality, while probing temporal change separately.

effect_name: Girls continuing in mathematics have more positive math attitudes
effect_claim: High-school girls who continue more years of math report more positive attitudes toward mathematics.
effect_claim_quote: Math enrollment groups differed significantly on the following scales: Usefulness of Mathematics, Confidence in Learning Mathematics
original_title: Continuing in Mathematics: A Longitudinal Study of the Attitudes of High School Girls
replication_title: Girls Talk About Mathematics and Their Future: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Girls Talk About Mathematics and Their Future: A Partial Replication
outcome_quote: girls continuing in math had more positive attitudes toward math
review_note: The same author partially repeats her earlier longitudinal comparison and again finds more positive math attitudes in girls who continue math study.

effect_name: Learning-disabled children underattribute failure to effort
effect_claim: Underachieving children assign less importance to lack of effort as a cause of their failures.
effect_claim_quote: underachievers believed lack of effort played less of a role in their failures than did control children
original_title: Learning Disabled Children's Attributions for Success and Failure
replication_title: LD Children's Attributions for Success and Failure: A Replication with a Labeled LD Sample
replication_target_quote: LD Children's Attributions for Success and Failure: A Replication with a Labeled LD Sample
outcome_quote: failure is not necessarily viewed as something that can be overcome with effort
review_note: Later paper repeats the attribution question in labeled learning-disabled children and reports the same general direction, but its abstract does not report the original between-group contrast.

effect_name: Expansive poses raise felt power
effect_claim: Adopting expansive rather than contracted postures increased self-reported feelings of power.
effect_claim_quote: increased feelings of power and tolerance for risk
original_title: Power Posing
replication_title: Power vs. persuasion: can open body postures embody openness to persuasion?
replication_target_quote: In the current study, we sought to replicate the finding that adopting an open/expansive body posture increases subjective feelings of power
outcome_quote: Results failed to replicate the previously found effect of body posture on subjective feelings of power.
review_note: The later authors name Carney, Cuddy, and Yap 2010 in their author-hosted manuscript, and test the original subjective-power endpoint. Later primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: First Step improves behavior in at-risk kindergarteners
effect_claim: The First Step to Success intervention improved behavior among at-risk kindergarten children.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicated a measurable intervention effect for both cohorts
original_title: First Step to Success: An Early Intervention Approach for Preventing School Antisocial Behavior
original_journal: Journal of Emotional and Behavioral Disorders
replication_title: First Step to Success: Replication and Social Validation of an Early Intervention Program
replication_journal: Journal of Emotional and Behavioral Disorders
replication_target_quote: the replication sample were nearly identical to those for the original field-test sample
outcome_quote: Results indicated that the replication was successful
review_note: Same intervention, kindergarten population, and two-cohort original field test; three overlapping authors. Crossref published-online dates April 1 and October 1, 1998, respectively. Later primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Sugar drink reverses impaired self-control
effect_claim: After an initial self-control task, consuming a glucose drink prevented impaired performance on a subsequent self-control task.
effect_claim_quote: consuming a glucose drink eliminated these impairments
original_title: Self-control relies on glucose as a limited energy source: Willpower is more than a metaphor
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Turn It All You Want: Still No Effect of Sugar Consumption on Ego Depletion
replication_target_quote: so-called ego-depletion effect is assumed to be alleviated by the consumption of sugar-containing drinks
outcome_quote: Results suggest that sugar consumption does not counteract ego depletion even when dissimilar self-control tasks are used.
review_note: Later paper explicitly cites Gailliot et al. 2007 as original support for glucose drink counteracting depletion and tests sugar vs artificial sweetener between two self-control tasks. Later primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Automated analysis aids interpretation of behavioral assessments
effect_claim: Automated nonparametric statistical analysis can support interpretation of functional analysis data.
effect_claim_quote: Results showed that exact behavior function agreement between ANSA and the publications authors was 83.1%, exact agreement between ANSA and PHVI was 75.4%, and exact agreement across all 3 methods was 64.6%.
original_title: Interpreting functional analysis outcomes using automated nonparametric statistical analysis
replication_title: Application of automated nonparametric statistical analysis in clinical contexts
replication_target_quote: Recently, Hall et al. (2020) provided a proof of concept for using automated nonparametric statistical analysis (ANSA) to interpret FA data.
outcome_quote: Our results were consistent with Hall et al.'s, indicating ANSA may augment clinical interpretation of FA data.
review_note: OpenAlex W3094555283 primary field Psychology. PubMed abstracts match exact DOI pair and later explicitly cites Hall et al. 2020.

effect_name: Repeated risk assessment improves prediction of recidivism
effect_claim: Recent repeated assessments of dynamic risk factors improve prediction of imminent criminal recidivism beyond initial scores.
effect_claim_quote: In this sample, reassessments consistently improved prediction as demonstrated by (1) incremental prediction over initial baseline scores and (2) improved model fit of the most recent assessment compared with the average of earlier scores.
original_title: Reassessment improves prediction of criminal recidivism: A prospective study of 3,421 individuals in New Zealand
replication_title: Does Reassessment Enhance the Prediction of Imminent Criminal Recidivism? Replicating Lloyd et al. (2020) With High-Risk Parolees
replication_target_quote: Lloyd et al. (2020) proposed and tested a novel three-step framework for examining the extent to which reassessment of dynamic risk and protective factors enhances the prediction of imminent criminal recidivism.
outcome_quote: The results of the previous study were largely reproduced: reassessment consistently enhanced prediction, with the most pronounced effects observed for a scale derived from theoretically acute dynamic risk factors.
review_note: Corrected wrong proposed Lloyd 2022 PNAS DOI to exact Lloyd et al. 2020 Psychological Assessment DOI 10.1037/pas0000813, confirmed in original PubMed and later SAGE primary abstracts. Later OpenAlex W3131119082 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Response interruption and redirection reduces vocal stereotypy
effect_claim: Response interruption and redirection reduced noncommunicative vocal stereotypy in children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: For each child, RIRD produced levels of vocal stereotypy substantially lower than those observed in baseline.
original_title: Assessing and treating vocal stereotypy in children with autism
replication_title: RESPONSE INTERRUPTION AND REDIRECTION FOR VOCAL STEREOTYPY IN CHILDREN WITH AUTISM: A SYSTEMATIC REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: This study systematically replicated and extended previous research on response interruption and redirection (RIRD)
outcome_quote: Results showed that RIRD produced substantial decreases in vocal stereotypy.
review_note: Corrected proposed same-issue 2011 link to exact Ahearn et al. 2007 target identified in later full-text Introduction. Later OpenAlex W1965505739 primary field Psychology. Same original effect label and claim as existing curated row; only vocal stereotypy reduction is claimed here, since appropriate vocalizations did not increase in later study.

effect_name: Income rank predicts life satisfaction beyond absolute income
effect_claim: A person’s income rank predicts life satisfaction even when absolute and reference income are considered.
effect_claim_quote: We find that the ranked position of an individual’s income predicts general life satisfaction, while absolute income and reference income have no effect.
original_title: Money and Happiness: Rank of Income, Not Income, Affects Life Satisfaction
replication_title: Buying Happiness in an Unequal World: Rank of Income More Strongly Predicts Well-Being in More Unequal Countries
replication_target_quote: we followed Boyce et al. (2010) and defined income rank
outcome_quote: Consistent with Boyce et al. (2010), the inclusion of income rank removed the effect of absolute income
review_note: The later study explicitly cites and follows Boyce et al. (2010), then repeats the income-rank association using Gallup data from 24 countries. It additionally tests moderation by inequality.

replication_title: Volitional saccade performance in a large sample of patients with obsessive‐compulsive disorder and unaffected first‐degree relatives
effect_name: OCD volitional saccade selection deficit in patients and unaffected relatives
effect_claim: Patients with OCD and unaffected first-degree relatives had slower volitional saccade response selection than healthy controls.
effect_claim_quote: Our results showed that unaffected first-degree relatives and OCD patients were significantly slowed compared to healthy comparison subjects in volitional response selection.
original_title: Impaired volitional saccade control: first evidence for a new candidate endophenotype in obsessive-compulsive disorder
original_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience
replication_target_quote: Recent evidence indicates that patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) as well as their unaffected first-degree relatives show deficits in the volitional control of saccades, suggesting that volitional saccade performance may constitute an endophenotype of OCD.
outcome_quote: In contrast to previous reports, neither patients nor relatives showed impairments in the performance of volitional saccades compared to healthy controls.
review_note: Corrected machine link from schizophrenia saccades to Kloft et al. 2012 OCD patients-and-relatives study. Later paper includes original coauthor Kloft and specifically retests the same familial volitional saccade endophenotype in a larger independent sample; both primary PubMed abstracts support the direction and result. Later primary OpenAlex field Psychology, checked before rate limit.

effect_name: Resurgence during reinforcement thinning
effect_claim: Destructive behavior commonly resurged as reinforcement schedules were thinned during functional communication training.
effect_claim_quote: We observed resurgence in 19 of the 25 (76%) applications of reinforcement schedule thinning.
original_title: Prevalence of resurgence of destructive behavior when thinning reinforcement schedules during functional communication training
replication_title: Prevalence of resurgence during thinning of multiple schedules of reinforcement following functional communication training
replication_target_quote: replicating previous research (Briggs et al., 2018)
outcome_quote: resurgence was observed in 97 of those steps (40.6%), similar to results of Briggs et al. (2018).
review_note: Corrected unrelated machine original to explicitly cited Briggs et al. 2018. Original 47/111 thinning steps (42%) and later 97/239 (40.6%) of the same FCT phenomenon; source Springer/Wiley primary abstracts. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Segmented instructional animation improves far transfer
effect_claim: Segmenting instructional animations improved students’ ability to apply teaching skills to new scenarios.
effect_claim_quote: SE groups outperformed no-SE groups on all learning measures
original_title: Optimising learning from animations by minimising cognitive load: cognitive and affective consequences of signalling and segmentation methods
replication_title: Impacts of segmenting principle on learner performance and attitude in a 3D environment: a mixed-method multiple case study
replication_journal: Journal of Computing in Higher Education
replication_target_quote: conceptual replication of Moreno’s (Appl Cogn Psychol 21:765–781. 10.1002/acp.1348, 2007) study
outcome_quote: Results indicate benefits for both cases in far transfer of learning.
review_note: Corrected machine original to Moreno 2007 exact DOI explicitly named in later abstract. Later 3D multimedia setting tests segmented instruction and finds far-transfer benefit in both synchronous and asynchronous cases. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Precognitive guessing of erotic image location
effect_claim: Participants purportedly guessed the future location of erotic pictures above chance, at a 53.1% hit rate.
effect_claim_quote: future position of the erotic pictures significantly more frequently than the 50% hit rate expected by chance: 53.1%
original_title: Feeling the future: Experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Raising the value of research studies in psychological science by increasing the credibility of research reports: the transparent Psi project
replication_target_quote: replication of Bem’s Experiment 1
outcome_quote: We found 49.89% successful guesses, while Bem reported 53.07% success rate, with the chance level being 50%.
review_note: Later exact-DOI PubMed Central paper and original published PDF identify Bem Experiment 1, erotic-picture location guessing, and incompatible hit rates; later OpenAlex primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Negative social events correlate with suicide indicators
effect_claim: Annual social stress scores were associated with attempted suicide in Hong Kong.
effect_claim_quote: this stress is associated with attempted suicide but not with diabetes mellitus or coronary heart disease.
original_title: Negative social events, stress, and health in Hong Kong.
replication_title: Social Stress and Suicide: Replicating an Asian Study with American Data
replication_target_quote: A study purporting to show an association between social stress and attempted suicide in Hong Kong
outcome_quote: social stress was positively associated with suicide rates.
review_note: The later American time-series repeats the social-stress test with a corrected regression and finds association with suicide mortality, whereas the original examined attempted suicide.

effect_name: Sex differences peak for casual partner criteria
effect_claim: In the original sample, men set lower mate-selection criteria than women for casual sexual relationships.
effect_claim_quote: Sex differences were greatest for casual sexual liaisons, with mens criteria being consistently lower than women's.
original_title: Integrating evolutionary and social exchange perspectives on relationships: Effects of gender, self-appraisal, and involvement level on mate selection criteria.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Evolutionary Theory and Mating Preferences: A Partial Replication of Kenrick et al.’s (1993) Study
replication_journal: Psi Chi Journal of Psychological Research
replication_target_quote: quantitative partial replication of Kenrick and colleagues’ (1993) analysis
outcome_quote: men and women were more similar than different.
review_note: Partial replication tests a selected subset of mate criteria and finds little of the broad sex-difference pattern; sample and measures differ.

effect_name: No bilingual advantage in prospective memory accuracy
effect_claim: The original Turkish-English bilingual group did not outperform monolinguals on prospective-memory accuracy.
effect_claim_quote: The results showed no direct evidence for a bilingual advantage in PM.
original_title: Do bilinguals have an advantage in prospective memory?
replication_title: Re-examining the Bilingual Advantage in Prospective Memory: A Partial Replication with Turkish Bilingual and Monolingual Young Adults
replication_target_quote: the present study offers a partial replication of Yörük et al.’s (2023) research investigating the effect of bilingualism on EB-PM
outcome_quote: consistent with the original study, provided no support for a bilingual advantage in PM accuracy.
review_note: Published 2026 partial replication by an original coauthor again finds no bilingual advantage in prospective-memory accuracy; it also changes the sample setting.

effect_name: Attractive online models increase weight-loss intentions
effect_claim: Exposure to attractive online model photos increased women’s planned weight-loss behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Participants exposed to attractive model pictures showed higher intentions, attitudes, and subjective norms to lose weight compared with unattractive models.
original_title: The Exposure Effects of Online Model Pictures and Weight-Related Persuasive Messages on Women’s Weight-Loss Planned Behaviors
replication_title: A replication and expansion of the exposure effects of online model photos and social comparison goals on planned behaviors and self-efficacy to lose weight
replication_target_quote: This study replicated and expanded social comparison theory predictions in regard to how exposure to online models
outcome_quote: Women and men exposed to online photos of more attractive models reported higher planned behaviors to lose weight relative to those who were exposed to photos of less attractive models
review_note: Same authors repeat the model-attractiveness comparison in an expanded sample including men and report the same direction for planned weight-loss behavior.

effect_name: Token rewards improve selected residential-treatment behaviors
effect_claim: Token reinforcement changed several appropriate and inappropriate behaviors in a home-style program for boys.
effect_claim_quote: The frequencies of aggressive statements and poor grammar decreased while tidiness, punctuality, and amount of homework completed increased.
original_title: ACHIEVEMENT PLACE: TOKEN REINFORCEMENT PROCEDURES IN A HOME‐STYLE REHABILITATION SETTING FOR “PREDELINQUENT” BOYS1
replication_title: REPLICATION OF THE ACHIEVEMENT PLACE MODEL IN CALIFORNIA1
replication_target_quote: Attempting to replicate procedures from Achievement Place
outcome_quote: Contingent point fines reduced the frequency of interruptions. Point rewards improved table-setting, but even large point rewards did not substantially increase savings.
review_note: California residential setting repeats Achievement Place token procedures; interruptions and table-setting improved, savings did not.

effect_name: Positive self-monitoring fails as criticism inoculation
effect_claim: Positive self-monitoring did not protect basketball learners from adverse effects of criticism in the original experiment.
effect_claim_quote: positive self-monitoring also decreased performance.
original_title: Criticism Inoculation Training: Concept in Search of Strategy
replication_title: Still searching for effective criticism inoculation procedures: An example of the value of replication and process analyses in applied sport psychology research
replication_target_quote: This study replicated and extended some aspects of the research reported by Kirschenbaum et al. (1984)
outcome_quote: As in the prior study, CIT proved surprisingly ineffective

replication_title: Self-Control Procedures in Modification of Smoking Behavior: Replication
replication_target_quote: method of modifying smoking behavior was replicated with an S
outcome_quote: The results suggest that the technique has applicability when undesirable emotional side effects are associated with efforts to stop smoking.
review_note: The original smoking-chair method reduced smoking in a single case; Roberts reports applying the same method in a person whose earlier quit attempts caused depression. Original full-text scan is available at the source URL.

effect_name: Group discussion shifts choices toward risk
effect_claim: Discussion in groups moves risk decisions toward greater risk under aversive consequences.
effect_claim_quote: group consensus achieved through discussion was displaced in the risky direction
original_title: Group decision making under risk of aversive consequences.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Dependence of the Risky Shift on Instructions: A Replication
replication_target_quote: An earlier study of group-induced shift toward risk was replicated
outcome_quote: usual (risk-oriented) instructions produced a shift toward risk while neutral instructions did not
review_note: The Michigan repository hosts the same Bem, Wallach and Kogan manuscript before its 1965 journal publication. The later paper repeats the group risky shift with usual instructions while adding a neutral-instruction condition.

effect_name: Working memory training improves fluid intelligence
effect_claim: Adaptive working memory training improved fluid intelligence scores on untrained tests.
effect_claim_quote: present evidence for transfer from training on a demanding working memory task to measures of Gf
original_title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Failure of Working Memory Training to Enhance Cognition or Intelligence
replication_target_quote: The current study attempted to replicate and expand those results by administering a broad assessment of cognitive abilities and personality traits to young adults who underwent 20 sessions of an adaptive dual n-back working memory training program
outcome_quote: no transfer of improvement was observed to any of the non-trained measurements
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Candidate original DOI omitted its final digit; exact Jaeggi et al. 2008 PNAS DOI confirmed by Crossref, Europe PMC, and the later PLOS full-text citation. Later paper used the same dual n-back task and failed to find transfer to fluid IQ.

effect_name: Future primes affect earlier response times
effect_claim: In retroactive priming, a later congruent prime was associated with faster earlier response times than an incongruent prime.
effect_claim_quote: participants were 15.0 ms faster on congruent trials than on incongruent trials
original_title: Feeling the Future: Experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Two Attempted Retro-Priming Replications Show Theory-Relevant Anomalous Connectivity
replication_target_quote: a large replication project of the retro-priming experiment by Bem and colleagues
outcome_quote: did not replicate Bem’s earlier findings of an anomalous interference of a future stimulus on response times.
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Candidate original DOI pointed to a different British Psychological Society item; exact Bem 2011 APA DOI confirmed by Crossref, Europe PMC and author-hosted PDF. Original quote is Experiment 3 full text, not the abstract; Experiment 4 reports the same direction.

effect_name: Assertiveness and communication apprehension share a factor
effect_claim: Items measuring assertiveness and communication apprehension share an interpersonal apprehension factor.
effect_claim_quote: The findings support the hypothesis that assertiveness is related to apprehension about communication.
original_title: A Factor Analytic Study of the Items in the Rathus Assertiveness Schedule and the Personal Report of Communication Apprehension
replication_title: Factor Analysis of the Rathus Assertiveness Schedule and the Personal Report of Communication Apprehension-24: Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: items for the Rathus Assertiveness Schedule and the Personal Report of Communication Apprehension share one common factor
outcome_quote: Only one common factor, apprehension in interpersonal contexts, was shared by items from both scales.
review_note: The shared interpersonal apprehension factor recurred with a revised communication-apprehension scale; other factor counts differed.

effect_name: Self-rated extraversion agrees with Eysenck scale scores
effect_claim: People rating themselves as introverted or extraverted differ accordingly on the Eysenck Extraversion scale.
effect_claim_quote: Results support the validity of the E scale of the E.P.I. when using Introvert and Extravert criterion groups as defined above.
original_title: Validity of the Eysenck Extraversion Scale as Determined by Self‐Ratings in Normals 1
original_journal: British Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: Validity of the Eysenck Extraversion Scale: Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: rated themselves and their peers on extraversion and filled out the Eysenck Personality Inventory
outcome_quote: Self-rated Introvert and Extravert criterion groups were significantly different from each other and from the total group on Extraversion score
review_note: The later study repeats the self-rated introvert/extravert group comparison on Eysenck Extraversion scores in a female college sample.

effect_name: All four humor styles show genetic and nonshared environmental influence
effect_claim: Both positive and negative humor styles in the UK twin sample reflected genetic and nonshared environmental influences.
effect_claim_quote: individual differences in all of them can be accounted for entirely by genetic and nonshared environmental factors
original_title: Genetic and Environmental Contributions to Humor Styles: A Replication Study
replication_title: A Behavioral Genetic Study of Humor Styles in an Australian Sample
replication_target_quote: thus replicating results previously obtained in a sample of twins from the United Kingdom
outcome_quote: additive genetic and non-shared environmental factors accounted for the variance in all four humor styles
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Machine-linked original DOI was the U.S. twin study, which found shared-environment effects for negative styles. Later Cambridge full text explicitly names Vernon et al. 2008a UK twin study as target and cites this corrected DOI; Australian results match its all-four genetic pattern.

effect_name: Switching between creative tasks improves RAT accuracy
effect_claim: Continually switching between creative tasks improved convergent problem-solving performance on Remote Associates Test problems.
effect_claim_quote: task switching can enhance two principal forms of creativity—divergent thinking (Study 1) and convergent thinking (Study 2)
original_title: “Switching On” creativity: Task switching can increase creativity by reducing cognitive fixation
original_journal: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
replication_title: Effects of task characteristics and task-switching on remote associates test problem solving
replication_target_quote: we conducted two studies to examine whether task characteristics and task-switching influence performance on Remote Associates Test (RAT) problems
outcome_quote: we did not replicate the positive effect of task-switching on RAT problem-solving accuracy found in previous studies.
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Original publisher abstract identifies convergent thinking Study 2; later full text explicitly cites Lu et al. 2017 for RAT task-switching accuracy. Later speed improvement is a distinct outcome; the target accuracy effect failed.

effect_name: Preschoolers give conjunctive interpretations of disjunction
effect_claim: Many preschool children treated disjunctive statements as if they meant conjunction in the original task setting.
effect_claim_quote: preschool children oftentimes understand disjunctive sentences as if they were conjunctive.
original_title: Children interpret disjunction as conjunction: Consequences for theories of implicature and child development
replication_title: Do Children Interpret ‘or’ Conjunctively?
replication_target_quote: Using stimuli modelled on previous studies, we test English-speaking preschoolers and replicate the finding that many children interpret or conjunctively.
outcome_quote: replicate the finding that many children interpret or conjunctively.
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Later study used stimuli modelled on the 2016 Singh et al. task and replicated the conjunctive response pattern. Its additional pragmatic-context manipulation largely eliminated the pattern, limiting the interpretation of a general semantic effect.

effect_name: Learned resourcefulness predicts cognitive therapy response
effect_claim: Depression patients higher in learned resourcefulness respond better to cognitive therapy than patients lower in resourcefulness.
effect_claim_quote: patients entering cognitive therapy with relatively high SCS scores did better than patients with low SCS scores.
original_title: Predicting response to cognitive therapy of depression: The role of learned resourcefulness
replication_title: Prescribing Therapy for Depression: The Role of Learned Resourcefulness, a Failure to Replicate
replication_target_quote: a high score predicting a good outcome with talking therapy and a low score a good outcome with drug therapy.
outcome_quote: Using the same paradigm, we predicted response correctly 7 times and incorrectly 16 times, a clear failure.
review_note: The original 35-patient study found a learned-resourcefulness by treatment interaction; the later 37-patient same-paradigm study failed to predict treatment response.

effect_name: Rats prefer warning of unavoidable shock
effect_claim: Rats prefer a warning light before unavoidable shock over a compartment where the same shock arrives without warning.
effect_claim_quote: Experimental Ss eventually spent 90% of the trials during acquisition in the compartment with the warning light
original_title: Choice of a warning signal or no warning signal in an unavoidable shock situation.
original_journal: Journal of Comparative and Physiological Psychology
replication_title: Preference for Warning in an Unavoidable Shock Situation: Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: To replicate and extend the previously reported preference for warning in an unavoidable shock situation
outcome_quote: All Ss exhibited a clear preference for the signal-shock condition, regardless of duration of warning.
review_note: Both papers tested rats choosing a warning signal before unavoidable shock; the later study extended warning durations from 3 to 30 seconds.

effect_name: Salvation primes increase work effort specifically among Americans
effect_claim: Implicit salvation cues increased work effort in Americans but did not do so in Canadians.
effect_claim_quote: Implicitly priming words related to divine salvation led Americans, but not Canadians, to work harder on an assigned task
original_title: Implicit Puritanism in American moral cognition
replication_title: A creative destruction approach to replication: Implicit work and sex morality across cultures
replication_target_quote: The present pre-registered empirical project compared the Implicit Puritanism account of intuitive work and sex morality
outcome_quote: Contradicting Implicit Puritanism's core theoretical claim of a distinct American work morality, a number of targeted findings replicated across multiple comparison cultures
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Original DOI is the Uhlmann et al. 2011 Implicit Puritanism article, confirmed by Crossref and author-hosted manuscript. Later paper explicitly says it directly replicated central effects from Uhlmann et al. 2011; findings across cultures contradicted the American-only work-morality claim.

effect_name: A few prolific liars tell most lies
effect_claim: Lying frequency is highly skewed, with a small minority accounting for a disproportionate share of lies.
effect_claim_quote: almost half of all lies are told by only 5% of subjects; thus, prevalence varies widely and most reported lies are told by a few prolific liars.
original_title: The Prevalence of Lying in America: Three Studies of Self-Reported Lies
replication_title: A few prolific liars in Japan: Replication and the effects of Dark Triad personality traits
replication_target_quote: This prediction, referred to as "a few prolific liars," is tested in Japan.
outcome_quote: Results indicate that the few prolific liars pattern is evident in Japan
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Machine-linked 2014 text-messaging article was not the study retested. Later PLOS full text names Serota, Levine and Boster 2010 U.S. adult survey in reference 7, with exact DOI; Japanese survey reproduced the skewed lie-count pattern.

effect_name: Self-relevance changes audiovisual numerosity judgments
effect_claim: Self-relevant information altered how auditory and visual event counts were combined in numerosity judgments.
effect_claim_quote: social relevance can influence multisensory processing at both perceptual and postperceptual stages
original_title: Social relevance modulates multisensory integration.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_title: Self as a prior: The malleability of Bayesian multisensory integration to social salience
replication_target_quote: Experiment 2 replicated the effects of social relevance on multisensory integration from Scheller & Sui, 2022 JEP:HPP
outcome_quote: the more frequently observed illusion (more malleable to prior influences) was modulated by self-relevance.
review_note: Directly names Scheller and Sui (2022); the later experiment used fewer events and tested a more frequent opposite illusion. Success is limited to self-relevance modulation, not identical absolute illusion rates.

effect_name: Infants predict an agent's action from its false belief
effect_claim: In a nonverbal toy-hiding task, 15-month-olds responded as if they predicted an actor's behavior from the actor's belief about the toy's location.
effect_claim_quote: we used a novel nonverbal task to examine 15-month-old infants' ability to predict an actor's behavior on the basis of her true or false belief about a toy's hiding place. Results were positive
original_title: Do 15-Month-Old Infants Understand False Beliefs?
replication_title: Infants attribute false beliefs to a toy crane
replication_target_quote: We conducted a replication of the violation-of-expectation procedure, except that the human agent was replaced by an inanimate agent.
outcome_quote: 16-month-old infants looked longer when it turned toward the object's new location, consistent with the attribution of a false belief to the crane.
review_note: Conceptual replication of Onishi and Baillargeon's 2005 violation-of-expectation task. A toy crane replaced the human actor; the infant looking-time pattern recurred, while the agent change limits the interpretation.

effect_name: Social context influences facial emotion judgments
effect_claim: Surrounding faces influenced Japanese participants' judgments of a central person's emotion, unlike Western participants in the original study.
effect_claim_quote: The surrounding people's emotions influenced Japanese but not Westerners' perceptions of the central person.
original_title: Placing the face in context: cultural differences in the perception of facial emotion
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Inferring Emotion from Facial Expressions in Social Contexts : A Role of Self-Construal?
replication_target_quote: attempted to replicate the findings of Masuda and colleagues (2008), testing a modified hypothesis
outcome_quote: The hypothesis was only (partially) confirmed for the emotional judgments of a neutral facial expression target.
review_note: Conceptual test of the proposed self-construal mechanism, using interdependence versus independence priming rather than Japanese versus Western samples. Partial result for neutral target; no systematic contextual incorporation across target emotions.

effect_name: Walking boosts divergent creative thinking
effect_claim: Walking increased scores on divergent-thinking tasks compared with sitting in the original experiments.
effect_claim_quote: Again, walking led to higher GAU scores.
original_title: Give your ideas some legs: The positive effect of walking on creative thinking.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
replication_title: Sensorimotor-Conceptual Integration in Free Walking Enhances Divergent Thinking for Young and Older Adults
replication_target_quote: In Experiment 1, we replicated previous findings with two additional groups of young participants.
outcome_quote: Only the free-walking group showed better performance in fluency, flexibility, and originality.
review_note: The later article cites Oppezzo and Schwartz (2014) and retests walking's benefit for divergent thinking; it compares free and constrained walking and extends to older adults. The successful code refers to free walking.

effect_name: Linguistic labels increase early visual P1 amplitude
effect_claim: Hearing object labels rather than equally informative nonverbal sounds increased the early visual P1 response to pictured objects.
effect_claim_quote: An analysis of ERPs showed that the P1 was larger when people were cued by labels compared with equally informative nonverbal cues
original_title: Words Jump-Start Vision: A Label Advantage in Object Recognition
replication_title: Words May Jump-Start Meaning More Than Vision: A Non-Replication of Early ERP Effects in Boutonnet and Lupyan (2015)
replication_target_quote: We report a replication of Boutonnet and Lupyan’s (2015) study of the effects of linguistic labelling on perceptual performance.
outcome_quote: We did not replicate the main ERP effects supporting a positive effect of linguistic labels on the early perceptual ERP components P1 and P2
review_note: Targeted the original early ERP label advantage, which failed. Behavioral label and congruence effects did replicate; this row concerns P1/P2 only. Original DOI verified by PubMed 26109657. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology ().

effect_name: Response-independent food induces stereotyped pigeon behavior
effect_claim: Pigeons given food at regular intervals independent of their actions developed repeated stereotyped responses that Skinner attributed to accidental reinforcement.
effect_claim_quote: If a clock is now arranged to present the food hopper at regular intervals with no reference whatsoever to the bird's behavior, operant conditioning usually takes place.
original_title: Superstition in the pigeon
replication_title: The "supersitition" experiment: A reexamination of its implications for the principles of adaptive behavior.
replication_target_quote: Replication and extension of Skinner's superstition experiment showed the development of two kinds of behavior at asymptote
outcome_quote: the development of two kinds of behavior at asymptote: interim activities (related to adjunctive behavior) occurred just after food delivery; the terminal response (a discriminated operant) occurred toward the end of the interval and continued until food delivery.
review_note: Later experiment observed repeated behavior under noncontingent food, but distinguished interim and terminal responses and rejected accidental reinforcement as a general explanation. Original DOI verified by PubMed 18913665. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology ().

effect_name: Family expressed emotion predicts depressive relapse
effect_claim: Relatives’ expressed emotion was associated with subsequent relapse among patients with depressive neurosis independently of other studied social and clinical factors.
effect_claim_quote: The expressed emotion of the relative again seems to be associated with relapse independently of all other social and clinical factors investigated.
original_title: The Influence of Family and Social Factors on the Course of Psychiatric Illness: A Comparison of Schizophrenic and Depressed Neurotic Patients
original_authors: Christine E. Vaughn and Julian P. Leff
replication_title: Expressed emotion, perceived criticism, and relapse in depression: a replication in an Egyptian community
replication_target_quote: The aims of this study were to determine the value of families' expressed emotion and patients' perception of family criticism in predicting relapse in Egyptian depressed patients
outcome_quote: The relation of family criticism to relapse was statistically significant.
review_note: Narrow effect is expressed family criticism predicting depressive relapse. Later found that relation significant, though its optimal criticism threshold differed and perceived criticism was null. Later Crossref reference list cites original DOI. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology (W2311551850).

effect_name: Costly apology and forgiveness after unintentional harm
effect_claim: When harm was explicitly unintentional, costly apologies increased perceived sincerity, while willingness to forgive did not significantly differ from apologies without cost.
effect_claim_quote: the willingness to forgive score did not significantly differ between the conditions
original_title: Do sincere apologies need to be costly? Test of a costly signaling model of apology
replication_title: Apology Cost Is More Strongly Associated With Perceived Sincerity Than Forgiveness
replication_target_quote: This study aimed at replicating a previously reported pattern: costly apologies are perceived as more sincere than non-costly apologies even when the transgression was unintentional, while costly apologies do not foster forgiveness more than non-costly apologies when the transgression was unintentional.
outcome_quote: Instead, we found that costly apologies promote not only perceived sincerity but also forgiveness in all three intention conditions.
review_note: Later paper explicitly identifies Ohtsubo and Watanabe (2009) Appendix as original target. Its own result says forgiveness also rose for costly apologies with no intent. Original published DOI verified through Kobe University repository/CiNii. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology (W4281715469).

effect_name: Elevated MMPI scales in borderline personality disorder
effect_claim: People diagnosed with borderline personality disorder showed higher elevations on six standard MMPI scales than other personality-disorder patients.
effect_claim_quote: The borderline group had higher elevations (p less than .05) on six of the 13 standard MMPI scales.
original_title: MMPI characteristics of the DSM-III borderline personality disorder
replication_title: Borderline personality disorder: Replication of MMPI profiles
replication_target_quote: The purpose of this study was to determine whether a particular MMPI profile is associated with borderline personality disorder (BPD).
outcome_quote: Concordance of MMPI profile for BDP confirmed the findings of four previous studies.
review_note: Later publisher references Gustin et al. (1983) explicitly and reports concordant elevated scales. Its abstract typo BDP is reproduced verbatim. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology (W2103299524).

effect_name: Standing reduces Stroop interference
effect_claim: Standing rather than sitting reduces response-time interference in the color-word Stroop task.
effect_claim_quote: the Stroop effect was smaller when participants were standing
original_title: Stand by Your Stroop: Standing Up Enhances Selective Attention and Cognitive Control
replication_title: Withstand control: standing posture differentially affects space-based and feature-based cognitive control through enhanced physiological arousal
replication_target_quote: the classic effect reported in the original study by Rosenbaum et al.
outcome_quote: We found evidence against an effect of standing posture on Stroop interference
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Later Nature full text directly identifies the Rosenbaum et al. 2017 Stroop RT effect and reports no posture x congruency interaction. Original author-hosted full text reports reduced interference while standing. The 2018 Sage corrigendum corrected outlier and order reporting but explicitly says the smaller standing Stroop effect was unaffected. Later study finds a separate Navon spatial-conflict benefit, so failure verdict is specific to Stroop RT.

effect_name: Conditioned evaluative meaning of nonsense syllables
effect_claim: Pairing nonsense syllables with meaningful words can condition their evaluative meaning.
effect_claim_quote: Strong language conditioning was obtained by this modified procedure by Es differing in age and status.
original_title: Meaning established by classical conditioning.
original_authors: Arthur W. Staats, Carolyn K. Staats, William G. Heard, Larry P. Nims
replication_title: Meaning Established by Classical Conditioning: Failure to Replicate
replication_target_quote: A classical conditioning procedure was used in which CS nonsense syllables were paired with UCS words of either positive, negative, or neutral evaluative meaning.
outcome_quote: Results indicated that there was no significant conditioning effect for any of the unaware Ss.
review_note: The 1959 report itself replicated a 1957 conditioning study and reported strong conditioning with multiple experimenters. Rozelle later found no effect among participants unaware of the pairings; the awareness exclusion limits the scope of failure.

effect_name: Performance expectancy influences answer revision
effect_claim: After low performance feedback, participants who were unexpectedly told they did well changed more answers than participants whose low feedback continued, consistent with preserving an expected level of performance.
effect_claim_quote: Subjects in the Low-High condition changed an average of 10.2 responses; the mean change in the Low-Low condition was 6.7.
original_title: Performance expectancy as a determinant of actual performance.
replication_title: Performance Expectancy as a Determinant of Actual Performance: Failure to Replicate
replication_target_quote: Their data supported the prediction that Ss would sabotage their own good performance in order to reduce cognitive dissonance.
outcome_quote: The present results for replicated and changed instructional groups were inconsistent with Aronson and Carlsmith's results.
review_note: Original primary article text reports 10.2 versus 6.7 answer changes in the low-expectancy conditions. The later experiment replicated part of the design and found results inconsistent with Aronson and Carlsmith. Primary paper scan is reproduced by Scribd.

effect_name: Irrelevant neuroscience enhances explanations for nonexperts
effect_claim: Naive adults and neuroscience students rated explanations containing logically irrelevant neuroscience as more satisfying.
effect_claim_quote: subjects in the two nonexpert groups additionally judged that explanations with logically irrelevant neuroscience information were more satisfying than explanations without
original_title: The Seductive Allure of Neuroscience Explanations
replication_title: Replicating the ‘seductive allure of neuroscience explanations’ effect in a classroom experiment and an online study
replication_target_quote: We thus decided to embark on a conceptual replication study of the original investigation.
outcome_quote: SNI boosting ratings mostly in participants with less expertise (p < 0.001), corroborating previous findings
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Royal Society full text explicitly identifies Weisberg et al. 2008 as the original investigation and describes conceptual replication. Machine-linked Fernandez-Duque et al. 2015 DOI is a different earlier replication. Weisberg original abstract in Yale-hosted PDF reports higher satisfaction from irrelevant neuroscience in nonexperts; later preregistered online study found SNI boost chiefly among less expert participants. Classroom arm varied and initially differed, so success applies to the larger online arm.

effect_name: Seen object handles automatically prime compatible actions
effect_claim: Pictures of graspable objects automatically facilitate compatible lateralized actions despite the handles being irrelevant to the task.
effect_claim_quote: seen objects automatically potentiate components of the actions they afford
original_title: On the relations between seen objects and components of potential actions
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
replication_title: Limits on action priming by pictures of objects
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
replication_target_quote: attempting to replicate a study reported by Tucker and Ellis (1998)
outcome_quote: the data provide no evidence for task-general automatic priming of lateralized responses by object handles
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Later NIH-hosted full text says Experiment 1a conceptually replicated Tucker and Ellis 1998 and Experiment 3b used their object list and closer procedure. The machine-linked 2000 micro-affordance DOI concerns grip and rotation rather than the original handle-side effect; canonical Crossref DOI for exact 1998 original uses one slash. Later study found priming only under explicit imagery instructions.

effect_name: Childhood resources moderate the effect of mortality cues on delay discounting
effect_claim: Mortality cues shifted preferences toward immediate rewards for those raised with fewer resources and toward delayed rewards for those raised with more resources.
effect_claim_quote: For individuals who grew up relatively poor, mortality cues led them to value the present and gamble for big immediate rewards. Conversely, for individuals who grew up relatively wealthy, mortality cues led them to value the future and avoid risky gambles.
original_title: The influence of mortality and socioeconomic status on risk and delayed rewards: A life history theory approach.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Does the thought of death accelerate a fast life history strategy? Evaluating a mortality salience prime
replication_target_quote: Griskevicius et al. (2011a) reported an interaction between childhood socioeconomic status and a mortality prime when measuring economic impulsivity using a delay-discounting task.
outcome_quote: no significant interaction between childhood environment and priming condition was observed.
review_note: The later paper's reference list identifies the exact Griskevicius et al. 2011a DOI 10.1037/a0022403. It changed mortality priming from a news article to open-ended writing and used a different delay-discounting measure, so the failed result is bounded to this retest.

effect_name: MAOA variants predict weak free-riding among women
effect_claim: Women carrying a low-activity MAOA variant were less likely to use weak free-riding strategies than women carrying the high-activity variant.
effect_claim_quote: Females with MAOA-L are less likely to behave like weak free-riders than MAOA-H carriers
original_title: Variants of the Monoamine Oxidase A gene (MAOA) predict free-riding behavior in women in a strategic public goods experiment.
original_journal: Journal of Neuroscience Psychology and Economics
replication_title: No association between genetic variants in MAOA, OXTR, and AVPR1a and cooperative strategies
replication_target_quote: we tested whether cooperative strategies were associated with three genetic variants thought to influence sociality in humans-MAOA-uVNTR, OXTR rs53576, and AVPR1 RS3.
outcome_quote: We found no association between cooperative strategies and any of the candidate genetic variants.
review_note: The later PLOS paper explicitly summarizes Mertins et al. (2013) as the prior MAOA/free-riding association and tests the MAOA variant in strategic public-goods behavior; its null result applies to its Chilean sample of 188. Original effect is female-specific, and later female-specific analyses also report no association.

effect_name: Tongue display deters social approach
effect_claim: Observers are slower or less willing to approach a person showing their tongue while occupied.
effect_claim_quote: The tongue-show affects an observer's willingness to interact
original_title: Experimental manipulation of a human non-verbal display: The tongue-show affects an observer's willingness to interact
original_authors: Kim G. Dolgin, John P. Sabini
replication_title: The Human Tongue Show and Observers' Willingness to Interact: Replication and Extensions
replication_authors: Nigel Jones, Judith Kearins, John Watson
replication_target_quote: Tongue showing and observers' willingness to interrupt was investigated in the laboratory with 48 male and 48 female subjects and 5 male and 5 female confederates.
outcome_quote: Significant latencies to interruption occurred with the tongue-show condition, a result consistent with 1982 work of Dolgin and Sabini.
review_note: The original 1982 result is stated in its finding-bearing title; no original abstract is available. The later abstract explicitly says the significant tongue-show interruption delay is consistent with Dolgin and Sabini (1982), and the publisher references the exact original paper. Its field extension also found fewer approaches to a tongue-showing seller.

effect_name: Spatially separated auditory tones impair spatial recall
effect_claim: Hearing tones from separate spatial locations during retention impairs immediate recall of spatial sequences.
effect_claim_quote: Spatial span recall was impaired if subjects saw visual targets or heard tones
original_title: Interference in immediate spatial memory
replication_title: Interference in immediate spatial memory: Shifts of spatial attention or central-executive involvement?
replication_journal: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology: Section A
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 replicated Experiment 2 by Smyth and Scholey (1994)
outcome_quote: Experiment 2 showed, however, that the effect of mere listening was not observed when this was the only interference condition experienced by the subject
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Later abstract explicitly identifies and reproduces Experiment 2 of Smyth and Scholey 1994: tone listening impaired spatial memory in its Experiment 1, but not in Experiment 2 when mere listening was the only interference condition. Later results also support central-executive rather than specifically spatial interference. The machine-linked Smyth 1996 paper is a different follow-up.

effect_name: Reward and punishment modify dominance in children
effect_claim: In paired schoolchildren, reinforcement combinations shifted dominant responding; both punishment conditions were stronger than reward without punishment, and all three conditions exceeded control.
effect_claim_quote: both punishment groups were more effective than reward-nonreward, but all 3 reinforcement combinations were significantly more effective than control
original_title: Modification of dominant behavior in school children.
original_authors: Elliot R. Blum, Wallace A. Kennedy
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Modification of Dominant Behavior in School Children: An Attempted Replication
replication_target_quote: The two purposes of this study were to determine the differential effectiveness of four combinations of reward and punishment on interpersonal dominant behavior and to see if any modification of responding would still be in evidence after an interval of 1 wk.
outcome_quote: Over 50 conditioning trials there was a significant increase in dominant responding by nondominant members, but none of the treatment groups was effective in bringing about this increase.
review_note: The original abstract reports all three reinforcement combinations stronger than control, with punishment conditions stronger than reward alone. The attempted replication changed the task and added an intrinsic-reward condition; dominance rose overall but no treatment condition produced the rise. Kennedy coauthored both studies.

effect_name: Translation distractors speed bilingual picture naming
effect_claim: A translation-equivalent distractor in the other language facilitates bilingual picture naming compared with an unrelated distractor.
effect_claim_quote: Naming was facilitated when the distractor was the name of the picture
original_title: Lexical Selection in Bilinguals: Do Words in the Bilingual's Two Lexicons Compete for Selection?
replication_title: Translation distractors facilitate production in single- and mixed-language picture naming
replication_target_quote: Here, in two experiments, we replicated and extended that effect
outcome_quote: Both experiments replicated previously reported translation facilitation effects in both single-language and mixed-language-response blocks
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Later PMC full text explicitly names Costa, Miozzo & Caramazza 1999 and states it replicated and extended their translation-facilitation effect, including the earlier mixed-language condition, with noncognate distractors. Original Elsevier abstract directly reports facilitation with different-language translations. Machine-linked 2017 Cognition paper is a different related investigation.

effect_name: Open hand prioritizes nearby visual targets

Later both experiments showed Simon effects regardless of cat presence; authors suggest the nearby experimenter may have supplied a competing spatial reference, so this failure is contextual rather than a claim that cat effects never occur. effect_name: Oral reading fluency varies by passage and not presentation order

Passage effect confirms; small significant order effect diverges from original null. 2018 is print issue year. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2770856851).

effect_name: Hijab use is associated with more positive body image
effect_claim: British Muslim women who wore the hijab reported more positive body image and less internalization of beauty ideals than nonwearers after adjustment for religiosity.

Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2606742552).

effect_name: Psychopathy facets have opposing links to negative emotionality
effect_claim: The interpersonal-affective facet of psychopathy was negatively associated with negative emotionality, while its social-deviance facet was positively associated.

Its supplemental factor-2 analyses also found positive NEM associations; instruments and sample differ.

effect_name: Video feedback improves sensitive limit-setting in parents of twins

The original author-hosted OSF PDF is a scanned page image; its first-page abstract was visually inspected, confirming the effect quote verbatim. Later study abstract reports all four original predictions replicated. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W4408581259).

effect_name: Three punishment-sensitivity profiles in Planets and Pirates

It found no association of profiles with obsessive-compulsive behavior, alcohol use, depression, or anxiety, an external-validity limit rather than failure of the exact three-profile effect. Machine-linked 2012 rumination and punishment-sensitivity paper is unrelated.

effect_name: Skilled typists prefer letter combinations typed with different fingers

This is a broader conceptual replication, with different cohorts and measurement. Both OpenAlex primary field Psychology. No causal gene claim is inferred.

Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W319148433).

effect_name: U-shaped oxytocin and trust association in men

effect_name: Chewing gum and lower perceived stress in worker surveys
