replication_authors: Jan Willem van den Berg, Jolanda J. Kossakowski, Wineke Smid, Kelly M. Babchishin, Denny Borsboom, Erick Janssen, Daan van Beek, and Luk Gijs
replication_target_quote: This study examined to what degree findings from previous network analyses, estimated using data from the Dynamic Supervision Project (N = 803; van den Berg et al., 2020), could be replicated.
outcome_quote: Dynamic risk factors general social rejection/loneliness, lack of concern for others, poor cognitive problem-solving, and impulsive acts showed high-strength centralities.
review_note: The 2022 authors compared original Dynamic Supervision Project data (N=803) against a distinct British Columbia corrections sample (N=4,511). The selected centrality pattern recurred, though global network structures differed; the outcome here is narrowly for the named centrality effect, not full network equality. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.
original_title: The Application of Network Analysis to Dynamic Risk Factors in Adult Male Sex Offenders
replication_title: Dynamic risk factors in adult men who committed sexual offenses: Replication and comparison of networks found in two independent samples.

effect_name: Bullying roles differ in perceived family power and cohesion patterns
effect_claim: Children categorized as bullies, victims, bully-victims, or controls showed characteristic differences in perceived family power and cohesion on the Family System Test.
effect_claim_quote: The four subgroups showed characteristic differences on the FAST plots
original_authors: Louise Bowers, Peter K. Smith, and Valerie Binney
replication_authors: Lia Berdondini and Peter K. Smith
replication_target_quote: A replication was made of the findings of Bowers et al.(1992)
outcome_quote: The findings regarding father absence, structural plot characteristics—such as use of corners and no separation of figures—and cohesion scores especially with parents, were consistent across both studies; findings relating to power scores were few and inconsistent.
review_note: The 1996 Italian sample retested 1992 British schoolchildren with a shared author but new participants. Original DOI looks unusual yet resolves to the exact Bowers et al. 1992 paper in OpenAlex (W2137583306). Consistent cohesion and structure but inconsistent power results make overall outcome mixed. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.
original_title: Cohesion and power in the families of children involved in bully/victim problems at school
replication_title: Cohesion and power in the families of children involved in bully/victim problems at school: an Italian replication

effect_name: Preventive cues produce superlearning in human causal judgments
effect_claim: A cue trained alongside a preventive cue drew stronger causal ratings than appropriate elemental acquisition and overshadowing controls.
effect_claim_quote: Experiment 1 demonstrated superlearning relative to appropriate control conditions.
original_authors: Kouji Urushihara and Ralph R. Miller
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Animal Learning and Cognition
replication_target_quote: previous research on superlearning (Urushihara & Miller, 2017) was replicated with the rating procedure changed slightly
outcome_quote: superlearning was clearly observed in comparison with two necessary control conditions, elemental acquisition control and overshadowing control.
review_note: A new 2022 human allergy-task experiment used outcome-magnitude ratings and explicitly retested the 2017 causal superlearning result. Same first author, distinct experiment and participants. Later paper is deposited by Kindai University, with English abstract in the author PDF. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. This is a peer-reviewed 2022 article in Applied Sociology Research Review 11(1), pp. 15–27; its DOI is deposited by Kindai University.
original_title: Causal superlearning arising from interactions among cues.
replication_title: An experimental analysis on superlearning in human causal judgement: A replication with rating of the outcome magnitude.
replication_journal: Applied Sociology Research Review, Kinki University

effect_name: Second-language speakers often misunderstand Miranda warnings
effect_claim: Most advanced English second-language speakers failed to understand their Miranda rights and performed worse on basic processing than native English speakers.
effect_claim_quote: most of our L2 participants failed to understand their Miranda rights and displayed significant disadvantages in basic level processing in comparison to native speakers.
original_authors: Aneta Pavlenko, Elizabeth Hepford, and Scott Jarvis
original_journal: International Journal of Speech, Language and the Law
replication_authors: Leigh Anne Benzaia, Scott Jarvis, Mary Akbary, and Hae In Park
replication_target_quote: This is a partial replication of Pavlenko et al. (2019), who demonstrated that non-native speakers of English generally fail to comprehend a common version of the Miranda warning.
outcome_quote: The results largely confirmed the findings of Pavlenko et al. while also suggesting that Miranda comprehension may be somewhat higher among the immigrant population in this study than in the population examined by Pavlenko et al.
review_note: The 2024 study explicitly used a different immigrant L2 population and an elicited-imitation measure. It confirmed widespread comprehension difficulty but found a higher comprehension rate than the 2019 original. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.
original_title: An illusion of understanding
replication_title: Investigating the relationship between L2 proficiency and Miranda rights comprehension: a partial replication of Pavlenko et al. (2019)
replication_journal: International Journal of Speech Language and the Law

original_title: Family preservation using multisystemic therapy: An effective alternative to incarcerating serious juvenile offenders.
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
effect_name: Multisystemic therapy reduces juvenile institutional placement
effect_claim: In a US randomized trial, juvenile offenders assigned to multisystemic therapy spent less time incarcerated than those receiving usual services.
effect_claim_quote: In comparison with youths who received usual services, youths who received MST had fewer arrests and self-reported offenses and spent an average of 10 fewer weeks incarcerated.
replication_target_quote: which has been effective at reducing out-of-home placements and producing favourable long-term clinical outcomes in the US.
outcome_quote: MST was more effective than CS at reducing youth internalising and externalising behaviours and out-of-home placements
review_note: US randomized trial N84 found about ten fewer weeks of incarceration with MST. Independent Norwegian randomized trial N100 found fewer out-of-home placements with MST. Placement measures and service systems differ.
replication_title: Multisystemic Treatment of Antisocial Adolescents in Norway: Replication of Clinical Outcomes Outside of the US

original_title: The Contribution of Therapist Effects to Patient Dropout and Deterioration in the Psychological Therapies
effect_name: Therapists differ in psychotherapy dropout rates
effect_claim: A UK clinical cohort showed meaningful variation in patient dropout across therapists, even after accounting for patient characteristics.
effect_claim_quote: Therapist effects accounted for 12.6% of dropout variance and 10.1% of deterioration variance.
replication_target_quote: as a replication and extension of recent findings regarding therapist effects on dropout.
outcome_quote: a therapist effect of 9.51% on dropout variance.
review_note: Original UK cohort: 10,521 patients and 85 therapists. Independent later US college counseling network: 10,147 clients and 481 therapists. Later full paper explicitly names Saxon et al. 2016 as a prior study replicated.
replication_title: Therapist effects on dropout from a college counseling center practice research network.

original_title: Priming the sexual system: Implicit versus explicit activation
effect_name: Subliminal sexual primes facilitate recognition of sexual targets
effect_claim: In men, subliminal sexual primes facilitated identification of sexual target pictures relative to neutral primes.
effect_claim_quote: Identification of sexual targets was facilitated by sexual primes, indicating that sexual representations in memory can be activated automatically.
replication_target_quote: In men, subliminally presented sexual pictures facilitated recognition of sexual information.
outcome_quote: A direct replication in women failed in Experiment 1.
review_note: Original male sample showed facilitation from subliminal sexual primes. Later independent female experiments failed in Experiment 1; Experiment 2 found facilitation only with male-oriented pictures. Cross-sex and stimulus-set changes limit interpretation.
replication_title: Nonconscious processing of sexual information: A generalization to women

original_title: Fear of self, doubt and obsessive compulsive symptoms
original_journal: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
effect_name: Feared-self beliefs predict obsessional doubt
effect_claim: Among nonclinical participants, stronger feared-self beliefs predicted more doubt in OCD-relevant checking and contamination vignettes.
effect_claim_quote: Higher levels of OCD symptoms and feared-self beliefs both significantly predicted both higher baseline levels of doubt and greater fluctuation in levels of doubt in both the contamination and checking scenarios, and to a much lesser extent in the control scenario.
replication_target_quote: This study aimed to partially replicate previous research that demonstrated a relationship between feared-self beliefs and obsessional doubt in OCD-relevant contexts.
outcome_quote: feared-self beliefs may partially contribute to heightened levels of doubt in response to possibility vs. reality-based information in OCD-relevant contexts.
review_note: Original paper online February 2015 studied N463 nonclinical participants. Later December 2015 paper describes a partial replication in an independent N221 nonclinical sample and supports the feared-self/doubt association in a checking vignette. This claim does not cover every original vignette or the new responsibility hypothesis.
replication_title: The Role of Fear of Self and Responsibility in Obsessional Doubt Processes: A Bayesian Hierarchical Model
replication_journal: Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology

effect_name: Reinforcement restores speech in long-term mute psychiatric patients
effect_claim: Operant reinforcement and imitation procedures re-established verbal responding in long-term mute psychotic patients.
effect_claim_quote: Verbal behavior was reinstated in 3 long-term, mute psychotics using reinforcement procedures.
replication_authors: Robert E. Pawlicki, Gary H. Miller, and Graham A. Haley
replication_target_quote: The present study replicated previous results showing the effectiveness of behavior-modification techniques in reinstating verbalization in mute psychotics.
outcome_quote: Those patients experiencing behavior-modification treatment increased their verbalization level significantly more than patients in either an attention-control or a no-treatment control group.
review_note: Publisher Crossref metadata for the 1973 article lists exactly two cited DOIs, including Sherman 1965 (10.1037/h0022148). Sherman's original abstract is visible in a preview of the original paper; PubMed confirms its DOI and bibliographic identity. Later patients were a new treated and control sample. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.
original_title: Use of reinforcement and imitation to reinstate verbal behavior in mute psychotics
replication_title: Increasing Verbalization of Chronic Mental Patients with Operant Techniques: Partial Replication

effect_name: Marital relationship patterns form types from RDI responses
effect_claim: Couples responses to the Relational Dimensions Instrument yielded an empirical typology of relationships.
effect_claim_quote: The second study derived an empirical typology of relationships based on couples' responses to the RDI.
original_journal: Annals of the International Communication Association
replication_target_quote: This paper describes an Australian replication of Fitzpatrick's marital typology.
outcome_quote: The three types were replicated and labelled connecteds, independents and separates.
review_note: The 1989 article explicitly cites the 1977 RDI development study and tests it in 190 new Australian couples. It reproduced three relationship types, with changes to two factor labels and one ideology effect. DOI metadata and publisher abstract confirm the 1977 original despite the online posting date 2017. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.
original_title: A Typological Approach to Communication in Relationships
replication_title: Fitzpatrick's Typology: An Australian Replication
replication_journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships

effect_name: Context paired with stronger deprivation increases later intake
effect_claim: Rats trained in a context under strong hunger later consumed more there than rats trained under weak hunger, despite no feeding in the training context.
effect_claim_quote: Measurement of food consumption showed the former high-drive group to consume significantly more food than the former low-drive group.
original_title: Establishment of a conditioned drive based on the hunger drive
original_authors: James S. Calvin, Elizabeth Ann Bicknell, and David S. Sperling
original_journal: Journal of Comparative and Physiological Psychology
replication_title: Establishment of a Secondary Drive Based on Thirst: A Replication
replication_authors: Sharen D. Enscore, Debra L. Monk, Frederick J. Kozub, and Kenneth A. Blick
replication_target_quote: In order to establish a secondary drive based on thirst
outcome_quote: the experimental Ss drank significantly more than the control Ss which indicated the presence of thirst fear in the experimental group.
review_note: 1976 paper is an explicitly titled replication adapting the 1953 conditioned-hunger design to thirst in a new group of rats. Publisher Crossref metadata for the later article cites exact Calvin/Bicknell/Sperling DOI 10.1037/h0060708. Original abstract is quoted from a paper preview hosted on ResearchGate; PubMed verifies later DOI and outcome. This is conceptual across primary drives. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Text hierarchy alone weakly predicts expository recall
effect_claim: Prominent main ideas in expository prose were better remembered in only one of the tested child grade and comprehension-measure conditions.
effect_claim_quote: Results revealed that in only one instance (third-graders responding to the multiple choice test) did the children respond in the predicted manner: greater comprehension of main idea, gist information.
original_title: Effect of Ideational Prominence on Children's Reading Comprehension of Expository Prose
replication_title: Ideational prominence and reading comprehension of expository prose: a partial replication
replication_target_quote: The present study partly replicated a study that found no evidence for a levels effect in children (Baumann, 1981) with a group of adults.
outcome_quote: With one passage stronger evidence for a levels effect was found with the adults in our study than was found with children, whereas with the second passage no evidence for a levels effect was found in either study.
review_note: The 1990 article explicitly names Baumann 1981 and tested new adult participants using two passages from the child study. The comparison is partial and cross-age: adults showed a stronger levels effect for one passage, none for the other, while the original child study showed little support overall. Outcome mixed, not a direct retest of child participants. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

original_title: The Relationship between Mindfulness and Uncontrollability of Ruminative Thinking
effect_name: Mindfulness buffers escalation of rumination
effect_claim: Higher dispositional mindfulness weakened the association between rumination and perceived uncontrollability in a student sample.
effect_claim_quote: mindfulness moderated the relationship between global levels of rumination and uncontrollability of rumination
replication_target_quote: to replicate a previous finding that mindfulness traits buffer the influence of causal analytic rumination on uncontrollability of rumination.
outcome_quote: there was no evidence that mindfulness traits prevent the development of rumination.
review_note: Original cross-sectional student sample N164 found mindfulness moderation. Independent Japanese student sample used cross-sectional and six-month longitudinal analyses (baseline N238, follow-up N114); it found no buffering moderation, although its exploratory Nonreact facet predicted lower later uncontrollability. The later full paper explicitly names Raes & Williams (2010); mindfulness measures differ.
replication_title: Do mindfulness traits prevent worsening of rumination？
replication_journal: Japanese Journal of Research on Emotions

effect_name: Demonstration increases realistic imaginary-object pantomimes in children
effect_claim: Four-year-olds shown a demonstration of an absent-object action produced more realistic pantomimes than children given verbal, practice, or imaginary-context prompts.
effect_claim_quote: The results showed that the demonstration group produced significantly more realistic responses than the other groups.
original_title: Zone of Potential Development for 4-Year-Olds Attempting to Simulate the Use of Absent Objects
original_journal: The Occupational Therapy Journal of Research
replication_title: Experimenter's Pantomimes Influence Children's Use of Body Part as Object and Imaginary Object Pantomimes: A Replication
replication_authors: Robert W. Mitchell and Heather Clark
replication_target_quote: This replication of Lyons's work (1983, 1986) examines whether different pretend contexts when requesting pantomimes influence children's use of IO and BPO pantomimes.
outcome_quote: Children produced, on average, the most IO pantomimes in the modeling context, fewer in the imaginary context, and the fewest in the request context.
review_note: The later publisher's Crossref references include Lyons 1986 DOI 10.1177/153944928600600103 and an undigitized Lyons 1983 dissertation. This pair uses the exact published 1986 experiment. The 2015 study tested 43 new children versus Lyons's 72 four-year-olds, with a comparable modeled-versus-context-versus-request ordering. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Listener emersion improves listener skills
effect_claim: After a listener emersion protocol, children with autism and severe language delays needed fewer trials to meet educational objectives.
effect_claim_quote: Following listener emersion the students required from one half to ten times fewer learn units to achieve objectives.
original_title: Acquisition of Fluent Listener Responses and the Educational Advancement of Young Children with Autism and Severe Language Delays
original_authors: R. Douglas Greer, Mapy Chavez-Brown, Anjalee S. Nirgudkar, Lauren Stolfi, and Celestina Rivera-Valdes
replication_title: Emergent Listener Fluency: A Replication
replication_authors: Ji Young Kim, Madeline R. Frank, and Daniel M. Fienup
replication_target_quote: Thus, we replicated the protocol by Greer et al. (2005) with three preschoolers with disabilities who had difficulty fluently responding to vocal directions.
outcome_quote: Results of this study indicate that listener fluency improved with an increased rate of correct responses across all 3 participants as a function of the listener emersion protocol.
review_note: The later open-access full paper explicitly says it replicated the Greer et al. 2005 listener emersion protocol in three new preschoolers. The original studied eight children and measured learn units needed for learning; this extension measures correct listener responses per minute, so the outcome concerns the shared listener skill rather than the identical dependent variable. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Distractors have little effect on trigram free recall
effect_claim: In Experiment II, adding distractors produced no statistically significant difference in free recall of CVC trigrams, though there was some suggestion of a handicap.
effect_claim_quote: NO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES WERE FOUND BUT THERE WAS SOME EVIDENCE TO SUGGEST THAT THE PRESENCE OF DISTRACTORS MAY HANDICAP FREE RECALL LEARNING.
original_title: An examination of recognition and free recall as measures of acquisition and long-term retention.
original_authors: Darryl Bruce and Charles N. Cofer
replication_title: Free recall of trigrams in the presence of distractors: A replication
replication_authors: Charles N. Cofer and Peter W. Dorfman
replication_target_quote: A replication of an experiment in which the influence of the presence of distractors on free recall of CVC trigrams was studied
outcome_quote: the influence of distractors on free recall, if any, is small
review_note: Later abstract explicitly reports a new experiment replicating the distractor comparison from Bruce and Cofer 1967 Experiment II, with largely agreeing small-effect result. Cofer overlaps as author but the later study is a new experiment, not reanalysis. The original Experiment II result is from an APA publisher preview hosted at ResearchGate. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

original_title: Japanese reactions to reward and punishment: a cross-cultural personality study
effect_name: Gray-Wilson sex differences on avoidance, flight, and approach
effect_claim: In a Japanese student sample, men scored higher on the Approach subscale and women on Flight and Active Avoidance.
effect_claim_quote: males were higher on Fight and Approach, while females were more disposed towards Flight and Active Avoidance.
replication_target_quote: Sex differences previously reported from the United Kingdom and Japan were replicated:
outcome_quote: Women scored significantly higher on the Active Avoidance and Flight subscales, men on the Approach subscale.
review_note: Independent Japanese college sample N597 and Indian Hindi-language university sample N437 show the same three specified subscale differences. The Japanese original also reported men higher on Fight; the later abstract does not claim that fourth result replicated.
replication_title: Hindi Translation of the Gray-Wilson Personality Questionnaire: A Cross-Cultural Replication of Sex Differences

original_title: The Misremembrance of Wines Past: Verbal and Perceptual Expertise Differentially Mediate Verbal Overshadowing of Taste Memory
effect_name: Verbal overshadowing depends on intermediate perceptual expertise
effect_claim: Describing a tasted wine impaired later recognition among untrained wine drinkers, but not novice non-drinkers or trained experts.
effect_claim_quote: As predicted, only the untrained wine drinkers showed impaired wine recognition following verbalization.
replication_target_quote: The results indicated that the act of verbalizing adversely affected recognition among those participants who had a greater perceptual expertise relative to their verbal expertise (i.e., the amateurs).
outcome_quote: verbalizing a previously-seen sequence of fencing movements improved subsequent recollection among novices but dramatically hindered recollection among intermediates, while having no effect on recollection among experts.
review_note: Exact source link is Melcher & Schooler 1996 wine expertise study, which the later PLOS full paper names and discusses; the machine-proposed Schooler 1990 paper is background to the generic phenomenon. Independent fencing sample N92 found intermediate-only impairment and no expert effect, but novice recognition improved rather than remaining unaffected. Stimulus modality and task differ.
replication_title: Verbal Overshadowing of Memories for Fencing Movements Is Mediated by Expertise

original_title: A comparative study of the general factor of personality in Jewish and non-Jewish populations
effect_name: Religious-affiliation contrasts in self-reported GFP scores
effect_claim: In three US surveys, respondents identifying as Jewish scored higher on the study-defined general factor of self-reported personality than comparison religious-affiliation groups; item differences tracked factor loadings.
effect_claim_quote: Analyses based on three large samples supported this hypothesis. Additionally, the Jewish/non-Jewish group difference on personality traits exhibited a Jensen Effect
replication_target_quote: Previously it was found that Jews residing in the United States have higher scores on the general factor of personality (GFP) in comparison to other religious groups.
outcome_quote: Mean level differences between religious groups were consistent with the previous findings, but the results of significance tests were more equivocal. Additionally, contrary to previous results, Jensen effects on the personality scale items for the group differences were not found.
review_note: Original used Add Health, MIDUS II, and Project Talent; later analyzed the distinct General Social Surveys. Mean pattern was similar but significance was inconsistent and the original item-loading association was absent. These are self-report associations in specific surveys; no causal, innate, or population-wide inference follows. Original first online Feb 10, later publisher dated Dec 1.
replication_title: Testing the Replicability of High Jewish Scores on the General Factor of Personality

effect_name: Faculty characteristics predict students’ perceived help with integrating psychology and faith
effect_claim: In a Christian clinical-psychology program, dimensions of faculty characteristics correlated with doctoral students’ ratings of faculty helpfulness in integrating psychology and faith.
effect_claim_quote: 2 of which correlated with students' assessment of how exemplary and helpful the faculty were
original_title: Doctoral Students' Integration of Psychology and Christianity: Perspectives via Attachment Theory and Multidimensional Scaling
original_journal: Journal for the Scientific Study of Religion
replication_title: How Students Learn Integration: Replication of the Sorenson (1997A) Model
replication_target_quote: replicating the Sorenson (1997a) study with students of the Graduate School of Psychology at Fuller Theological Seminary
outcome_quote: Results indicate that Fuller students learn integration the same way Rosemead students do.
review_note: Original journal abstract reports a 48-student Rosemead sample and faculty dimensions linked to helpfulness; the later publisher abstract explicitly retests the Sorenson 1997a model in independent Fuller students. Later OpenAlex W2792897442 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Young adolescents can describe personal meaning in life
effect_claim: Young adolescents can coherently describe what gives their lives meaning in free-response reports.
effect_claim_quote: the percentage seeming to understand what meaning in life was and able coherently to discuss their own was just as high as that found in older groups
original_title: Young Adolescents' Meaning in Life
replication_title: Adolescents' Meaning in Life: A Replication of Devogler and Ebersole (1983)
replication_target_quote: we examined how religious adolescents differ in their self-reports of meaning in life compared to adolescents previously studied
outcome_quote: 81 adolescents from a religious summer camp reported commitment to a belief as their strongest personal meaning more frequently than any other category when reported in a free-response essay format
review_note: The original SAGE abstract reports that 116 adolescents could describe personal meaning; the later SAGE abstract explicitly cites the earlier De Vogler–Ebersole study and obtains free-response accounts from an independent religious-camp sample of 81. The core reportability finding recurs; category distribution differs by sample, and no adult comparison was retested. Later OpenAlex W2106601116 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Matching parental differential-treatment patterns are most common
effect_claim: In preschool-sibling families, mothers and fathers most often showed congruent patterns of differential treatment.
effect_claim_quote: Congruent patterns of differential treatment (i.e., mothers and fathers showed the same pattern) were the most frequent.
original_title: The Family Correlates of Maternal and Paternal Perceptions of Differential Treatment in Early Childhood
replication_title: Family Relationships and Children's Emotional Adjustment as Correlates of Maternal and Paternal Differential Treatment: A Replication with Toddler and Preschool Siblings
replication_authors: Brenda L. Volling and Julie L. Elins
replication_target_quote: This study attempted to replicate the findings of McHale, Crouter, McGuire, and Updegraff and also of Volling
outcome_quote: Congruence in mothers' and fathers' reports of differential treatment (i.e., similar treatment from both mother and father) was most frequent.
review_note: The later paper explicitly attempts to replicate Volling 1997 as well as McHale et al. 1995, using a new sample of 60 families with toddler/preschool siblings. This pair is specifically the congruent-pattern prevalence result from Volling 1997; a separate existing Retested pair links the same later paper to McHale et al. on marital distress. Other outcomes in the later study differ by developmental age. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Self-generated sound cues aid word retrieval in aphasia therapy
effect_claim: Teaching a deep dyslexic patient to generate initial word sounds facilitated spoken naming.
effect_claim_quote: Spoken naming was also facilitated as information on the written form of the word could similarly be used to provide a phonemic cue for spoken production.
original_title: The autocue? self-generated phonemic cues in the treatment of a disorder of reading and naming
replication_title: Deficit-oriented treatment of word-finding problems: Another replication
replication_authors: Roelien Bastiaanse, Margreet Bosje, and Marjolein Franssen
replication_target_quote: A similar symptom complex has been described and successfully treated by Bachy-Langedock and De Partz (1983) and Nickels (1992). We replicated their therapy methods and evaluated the effects.
outcome_quote: Improvement was found in treatment-related, but not in unrelated tests. This improvement generalized to spontaneous speech.
review_note: Exact original Nickels 1992 DOI is from the author university research portal, correcting the unrelated machine-selected 1991 sentence-processing paper. A new 1996 patient received the cited therapy approach. Both studies report improvements on trained word-retrieval/reading measures while neither restored nonword reading; successful is restricted to the word-retrieval cue effect. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

original_title: Divided attention performance and the matching law
effect_name: Relative reinforcement increases stimulus dimension discriminability
effect_claim: In pigeons, accuracy or discriminability for a compound stimulus dimension rose with that dimension's relative reinforcement rate.
effect_claim_quote: Variations in relative accuracy with changes in relative reinforcement were well described by the generalized matching law.
replication_target_quote: replicating the results of Shahan and Podlesnik (2006)
outcome_quote: Discriminability, measured by log d, for stimuli on a dimension increased as the relative frequency of reinforcers for that dimension increased
review_note: Systematic, explicitly named replication in four new pigeons, with a different compound stimulus pair and symbolic rather than identity matching-to-sample. It replicates the graded relation between relative reinforcement and discriminability, not the original quantitative model.
replication_title: Divided stimulus control: a replication and a quantitative model
replication_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

original_title: Individual differences in valence modulation of face-selective M170 response
effect_name: Fearful-face detection sensitivity correlates with trait anxiety
effect_claim: Among healthy adults, better masked fearful-face detection sensitivity was associated with higher trait anxiety.
effect_claim_quote: Subjects who were better able to detect fearful faces also showed higher trait anxiety levels.
replication_target_quote: one recent study showed that fearful face detection sensitivity correlated with trait anxiety in healthy adults
outcome_quote: Replicating previous results, we found a significant positive correlation between trait anxiety and fearful face detection sensitivity.
review_note: The original behavioral correlation used the eight trait-anxiety-tested volunteers from a 31-person MEG study; the later paper describes recruiting 21 healthy volunteers through NIH community email advertisements for a masked-face behavioral study. Later authors explicitly identify Japee et al. 2009 and repeat the trait-anxiety association; state-anxiety and other traits are extensions. Newly recruited 21-person cohort is treated as distinct from the earlier MEG study.
replication_title: Fearful face detection sensitivity in healthy adults correlates with anxiety-related traits

effect_name: Money reminders increase self-sufficient focus
effect_claim: Money primes promote a self-sufficient orientation and greater focus on oneself than on others.
effect_claim_quote: money brings about a self-sufficient orientation in which people prefer to be free of dependency and dependents
original_title: The Psychological Consequences of Money
replication_title: The Effect of Money Priming on Self-Focus in the Imitation-Inhibition Task
replication_journal: Experimental Psychology (formerly Zeitschrift für Experimentelle Psychologie)
replication_target_quote: we tested the core assumption underlying the self-sufficiency hypothesis (i.e., money primes lead to an increased focus on the self; Vohs et al., 2006)
outcome_quote: a preregistered high-powered experiment replicated this effect, suggesting that money primes may indeed increase a focus on the self.
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. This is a conceptual test of the original self-sufficiency claim using implicit imitation-inhibition rather than the original help/social-distance measures. Later registered report notes effects are small and order effects limit confidence.

effect_name: Warm therapeutic packs increase prosocial gift choices
effect_claim: Holding a warm rather than cold therapeutic pack made participants more likely to choose a gift for a friend instead of themselves.
effect_claim_quote: participants holding a hot (versus cold) therapeutic pad were more likely to choose a gift for a friend instead of for themselves
original_title: Experiencing Physical Warmth Promotes Interpersonal Warmth
replication_title: Replication of “Experiencing Physical Warmth Promotes Interpersonal Warmth” by Williams and Bargh (2008)
replication_target_quote: three high-powered, independent replications of Study 2 from Williams and Bargh (2008)
outcome_quote: We did not replicate the effect in any individual laboratory or when considering the results of the three replications together (total N = 861).
review_note: The later journal abstract names original Study 2, matches hot/cold therapeutic packs and prosocial reward choice, and reports three independent laboratories (N=861). OpenAlex W2129480442 primary field Psychology. A 2017 article by overlapping authors reanalyzes a subsample of these same participants and should not be counted separately.

original_title: Learning Without Awareness by Academic and Nonacademic Samples: An Individual Differences Study
effect_name: No detected implicit determiner learning in noncollege adult sample
effect_claim: Among noncollege adults in the original semi-artificial L2 task, the authors found no evidence of implicit determiner learning on trained or generalization items.
effect_claim_quote: exhibited no evidence of learning regardless of the item type
replication_target_quote: replicating Kim et al. (2023)
outcome_quote: no evidence of implicit learning was found among unaware learners—replicating Kim et al. (2023)
review_note: The 2023 original reports no detected learning among nine nonacademic participants and cautions that its small sample gives wide intervals; the 2025 fully remote study enrolled 49 adults without college degrees and likewise reports no evidence among unaware learners. This is a replication of a null finding, not evidence that learning is impossible. Later source explicitly names the original; distinct study modality and newly recruited sample.
replication_title: A Bayesian approach to implicit L2 learning: Web-based replication of Williams (2005) and Kim et al. (2023) with underrepresented learners

effect_name: Infants expect agents to act on false beliefs

effect_claim: Exerting self-control on one task reduces performance on a subsequent task that requires self-control.

original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: No ego-depletion effect without a good control task
replication_target_quote: we tried to replicate the ego-depletion effect using a 30-min modified Stroop task
outcome_quote: In the first study, we compared the performance of a handgrip endurance task after this depleting task or after a classic control task (i.e., reading color words) and failed to replicate the ego-depletion effect. We showed that the control task induced boredom and subjective fatigue. In a second study, we looked for a better control task and compared the color-word reading task to another possible control task used in the literature (i.e., watching a documentary). Controlling for boredom, subjective fatigue, motivation and affective state, we found that the video task was not boring and did not induce fatigue, drop in motivation or negative affective state, whereas the color-word reading task did. In a third study, we used the video task as the control task and the modified effortful Stroop task used in the first study as the depleting task and succeeded in replicating the ego-depletion effect.
review_note: Independent conceptual replication of the Baumeister et al. 1998 sequential two-task ego-depletion effect, explicitly cited in later full text. Experiment 1 (Stroop vs boring color-word control then handgrip) failed; Experiment 3 (Stroop vs documentary control then handgrip) succeeded. Different task sequence than 1998 and control-task boredom materially changes result. Untrusted pool linked to a 2012 review instead of empirical original; corrected to Baumeister et al. 1998. The later paper intentionally reversed familiarization from possible to impossible events, so the direction of infants' event preference changes by design and is not treated as a replicated behavioral effect. This pair is limited to the empirical result that time-locked pupil data resolves ambiguity left by cumulative looking times; both primary abstracts state that result, and the later full paper details it.
